model: Sum-of-parts: owner-FCF DCF on ex-REA operations plus 62% REA Group stake at market (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: 62.0% REA Group stake at market (81.1m REA shares x A$154.63 x 0.6929 AUDUSD, ASX close 2026-10-01)
equity_bridge.note: 81.1m = 62.0% of ~131m REA shares outstanding after REA's FY2026 A$200m buyback (REA FY2026 FCF A$765m / A$5.80 per share = 131.9m weighted). REA 52-week range A$131-233; the stake is marked 33% below REA's high. No holdco discount applied; no CGT applied (no sale assumed). Flex: each A$10 on REA is ~US$1.03/NWS share.

equity_bridge.item: Less REA Group's 20% of Move (realtor.com), already inside REA's market value
equity_bridge.note: Move FY2026 revenue $610m at ~breakeven Segment EBITDA; 20% of an assumed ~1.5x revenue (~$900m) value. Keeps Move at News Corp's ~92% effective economic share.

equity_bridge.item: Non-REA investments: ~6% DAZN stake (Foxtel consideration), China investments, News UK/DMG Media JV
equity_bridge.note: 10-K Note 6: total investments $1,002m = equity method $95m + equity and other securities $907m; the securities line also holds REA's Athena Home Loans and Nexxen stakes (excluded, inside REA's market value). ~$870m non-REA book taken at ~70% because DAZN is private and loss-making and the China holdings are illiquid.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: segment-weighted FY2026 organic growth of the ex-REA businesses (Dow Jones +7%, Book Publishing +4-5% organic, News Media -1% organic, Move +11%), decelerating; the equity CAGR is not usable here
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.1% 3yr, 0.2% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS (58% 3yr off an impairment-depressed FY2023 base) and from revenue. Book value is suppressed by $0.9bn of buybacks and dividends over FY2024-26 and by the Foxtel disposal; EPS is distorted by restructuring/impairment swings. Neither is a growth anchor. Revenue 5yr CAGR is negative only because FY2021 includes Foxtel (discontinued from FY2025).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC: FY2021 $847m-$128m=$719m; FY2023 $745m-$87m=$658m; FY2026 $811m-$77m=$734m), consolidated basis because the REA split is only available for FY2026. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR 3.7% vs reported-FCF 3yr CAGR 2.9%: SBC fell from $87m to $77m, so owner FCF grew slightly faster than reported FCF; SBC is not outpacing cash flow at News Corp. FY2021-22 FCF includes Foxtel.

scenario_narratives.base: The ex-REA group grows ~3% a year, led by Dow Jones (digital subscriptions, Risk & Compliance data, AI content licensing) with HarperCollins steady and News Media shrinking slowly in print while adding UK digital subscribers and licensing income. Segment margin expands from 11.6% toward ~14% by FY31-32 as management has signalled, with ~1pp a year of restructuring cash charged against it as a recurring cost of running down print. Move stays around breakeven, improving slowly. The REA stake is carried at its 2026-10-01 market value; its own cyclicality (Australian listings and mortgage rates) is marked by the ASX, not re-modelled here.
scenario_narratives.bull: Dow Jones reaches its $1bn EBITDA target by FY31 with Risk & Compliance compounding mid-teens and AI licensing scaling as a near-pure-margin line; Move becomes solidly profitable on premium agent products; News Media's restructuring completes and the segment stabilises. Ex-REA adjusted margin reaches 15.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI disintermediation of news traffic outruns licensing income, Dow Jones slows to low-single-digit growth with a flat margin, print declines accelerate, Move keeps losing share and money, and HarperCollins is a flat backlist annuity. Ex-REA revenue is roughly flat for a decade and adjusted margin slips to 9.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sum-of-parts. The 62% REA Group stake is a liquid, separately listed asset worth ~US$8.7bn at market (half of News Corp's own market cap), so it is taken at its ASX price rather than re-modelled inside a consolidated DCF where it would be charged at 100% of its cash flows against a book NCI worth a tenth of its market value. The remaining operations (Dow Jones, HarperCollins, News Media, Move, corporate) are valued on a strict owner-FCF basis: SBC expensed, the share count held flat, operating leases charged in the margin, recurring restructuring cash charged in the margin, terminal value the lower of Gordon at 2.5% and 15x FCF. The implied question for the buyer is what the market is paying for the ex-REA stub: at the NWS price the stub trades at roughly 8-9x Segment EBITDA, which is cheap for Dow Jones alone and about right once News Media's melting ice-cube and Move's losses are blended in.
key_risks_to_valuation: REA Group share price: the stake is marked at A$154.63 (33% below its 52-week high); each A$10 move is ~US$1.03 per NWS share, and REA's own exposure to Australian listing volumes and mortgage rates is not scenario-flexed here

AI disintermediation of search referral traffic to WSJ and the mastheads versus the durability of AI content-licensing fees (OpenAI, Meta, Bloomberg); Google litigation and subpoenas on licensing records
Secular print decline at News Media; restructuring cash is charged at ~1.1pp of revenue a year and could run higher
Move/realtor.com remains loss-making or near breakeven against Zillow and CoStar; the bridge assumes a ~$900m value for REA's 20% deduction
DAZN stake carrying value (~6% of a private, loss-making sports streamer) is taken at a ~30% haircut to book; it could be worth zero

Dual-class control (LGC Holdco / Lachlan Murdoch at ~34.5% of Class B) and the ~10% Class B voting premium over NWSA: the per-share value is the same for both classes, so the NWS line carries a premium the model does not value
AUD and GBP translation: a one-cent AUDUSD move is ~$37m of revenue and ~$12m of Segment EBITDA (10-K), largely REA

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, Nasdaq regular close at inputs.price_as_of (Class B NWS; Class A NWSA same session); 52-week range 25.49-35.76. REA.AX from the same API, ASX close same day; AUDUSD=X 0.6929 same day.
data_sources.financials: News Corp Form 10-K FY2026 (filed 2026-08-07, period 2026-06-30): segment table, DRES REA/Move revenue split, cash-flow statement, Notes 6, 9, 13, 14; SEC XBRL companyfacts for FY2024-26 cross-checks; NWS_Metrics.csv (82 periods, XBRL-derived). REA Group FY2026 A$ figures (OCF, capex, capitalised development, SBC, FCF/share, operating income) from stockanalysis.com ASX:REA statements, translated at ~0.67 FY2026 average AUDUSD.
data_sources.qualitative: NWS_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): segment outlook, Dow Jones $1bn EBITDA target, FY2027 margin-expansion and mortgage-rate commentary from the Q4 FY2026 release; 10-K risk factors.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 consolidated revenue $9,028m less REA Group revenue $1,406m (10-K FY2026 DRES discussion). The flows below are Dow Jones + Book Publishing + News Media + Move (realtor.com) + corporate. REA Group is carried in equity_bridge at market, not in the flows.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted, both classes: 360,503,747 Class A (NWSA) + 180,548,891 Class B (NWS) outstanding at 31 July 2026 (10-K cover) = 541.05m, plus 1.9m dilutive effect of equity awards (10-K Note 14 FY2026). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Class A and Class B have identical economic rights; the per-share value applies to either class. The quoted price is the Class B (NWS) line, which trades ~10% above NWSA (28.64 same close) for its vote.
inputs.net_debt_note: Debt is News Corp's own borrowings (2021/2022 Senior Notes + 2026 Term A Loans, $1,989m, XBRL LongTermDebt 2026-06-30; REA's A$200m facility was fully undrawn). Cash is consolidated $2,095m less $255m held by REA Group (10-K liquidity section: 'not readily accessible... held by REA Group'), because REA's cash is inside REA's market value in the bridge. Operating lease liabilities ($926m) are NOT in net debt: US GAAP operating lease cost ($109m FY2026) sits inside Segment EBITDA, so the lease is charged in the flows (treatment B).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Ex-REA free cash flow: consolidated FY2026 FCF $811m (OCF from continuing ops $1,237m less capex $426m, 10-K reconciliation) less REA Group FCF of ~$423m (REA FY2026 OCF A$771m less PP&E capex A$6m and capitalised development A$134m = A$631m, at ~0.67 FY2026 average AUDUSD). FY2026 ex-REA FCF carries a ~$145m consolidated working-capital outflow (an improvement on FY2025's -$206m, per the Q4 release) and ~$90m of restructuring cash; restructuring is treated as recurring in the margin path rather than normalised away.
inputs.interest_income_note: Ex-REA net debt is ~$149m, i.e. net cash is not material (rule: strip interest only when net cash > 1x FCF base). Consolidated 'Interest income, net' was +$29m FY2026; nothing is stripped.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2026 Note 13: total equity compensation expense $77m (FY2025 $84m, FY2024 $91m), less REA Group's own share-based payments of A$16m (~$11m) which belong to the REA stake. No separate equity-award tax withholding line is disclosed in financing; PSU/RSU settlement note says settlement values exclude statutory withholdings, so the $66m is the expense figure only.
inputs.buyback_note: Actual FY2026 repurchases of News Corp shares $641m (cash flow statement), up from $150m FY2025, under the $1bn program authorised Jan-2026 (ASX daily notices filed as 8-Ks). Repurchaser: the flat count is being funded. Dividends paid $204m FY2026. REA Group separately repurchased A$200m of its own shares.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: ~4.2% 10y UST + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.0 gives ~9.2% cost of equity; ~$2.0bn of debt at ~4.5% pre-tax against ~$16bn market cap pulls the blend to ~9.0%. Below the 10.5% US-tech house default because the ex-REA mix is mature subscription/publishing with low capital intensity, and above a utility-like rate because News Media is in secular decline. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, in the flows.
inputs.lease_treatment: B: operating lease cost (~$109m FY2026, 10-K lease note) is inside Segment EBITDA and therefore inside the modelled margin; operating lease liabilities ($926m) excluded from net debt. Not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, by exclusion: REA Group (62.0% owned, ASX: REA) is removed from the flows entirely (revenue, EBITDA, D&A, capex, SBC, cash) and News Corp's 81.1m REA shares are added in equity_bridge at the 2026-10-01 ASX close. REA's 20% of Move is deducted in the bridge so Move is counted at News Corp's effective ~92% economic share. No other NCI is material once REA is out. Book NCI $710m (2026-06-30) is almost entirely REA and is not deducted again.
inputs.notes: MODEL: sum-of-parts. News Corp straddles two routing rows: an operating company (Dow Jones, HarperCollins, News Media, Move) and a holdco for a 62% stake in a separately listed company (REA Group) whose market value (~US$8.7bn) is about half of News Corp's own market cap. A consolidated owner-FCF DCF would either count REA's cash flows at 100% and deduct a book NCI that is one-tenth of its market value, or require an attributable leakage rate that is really just REA's market multiple in disguise. So: owner-FCF component DCF on ex-REA flows (this file's drivers), plus REA at market in the bridge. Per SKILL.md 'value the parts separately and sum, and say so'. EBITDA MARGIN PATH is Segment EBITDA less ~1.1pp of revenue for recurring restructuring/impairment cash: News Corp has booked $133m/$132m/$113m of impairment and restructuring in FY2024-26 and the News Media footprint will keep generating severance; FY2026 ex-REA Segment EBITDA margin was 11.6% ($887m / $7,622m; Dow Jones $663m + Books $287m + News Media $139m + Move ~breakeven - corporate $203m), so the FY0 adjusted anchor is ~10.3-10.5%. Move EBITDA is inferred at ~breakeven from DRES Segment EBITDA $741m less REA EBITDA ~A$1,100m x 0.67. FOXTEL: sold to DAZN 2 April 2025; discontinued operations in all periods, so FY2025 revenue/FCF and all CAGRs that reach back to FY2022 mix Foxtel-in and Foxtel-out bases. DAZN stake (~6%) is in the bridge. Price volatility: regular close, not after-hours. Weighted IV is per economic share of either class; compare to NWSA (28.64) for the no-vote line.

bear.narrative: AI answer engines erode the search-referral funnel for WSJ and the UK/Australian mastheads faster than licensing deals replace it; Dow Jones growth halves to ~3-4% and its margin stalls; print advertising declines accelerate so News Media drops toward breakeven despite continuing severance; Move loses share to Zillow/CoStar and stays loss-making; HarperCollins reverts to a flat, 12%-margin backlist business. Adjusted margin slips to 9.5% and revenue barely grows. Same WACC and cap: the pessimism is in the flows, not the rate.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 3.6% = Dow Jones +7% (digital subs + Risk & Compliance + AI licensing), Books +3% (FY26 had $31m of acquired revenue and a hit-driven frontlist), News Media -1% organic (print decline offset by UK digital and licensing), Move +8%; weighted on FY26 revenue. Decelerates to 2.2% as Dow Jones matures and print keeps shrinking.
base.margin_rationale: Segment EBITDA margin less ~1.1pp recurring restructuring cash. FY26 anchor 10.3-10.5% adjusted (11.6% Segment). Management expects further margin expansion in FY27 and targets Dow Jones EBITDA of $1bn within five years (FY26 $663m); the base gets Dow Jones to ~$0.9bn by FY31 and holds Books ~13%, News Media ~6%, Move drifting to a small profit, corporate ~-$215m. Ends at 13.0% adjusted (~14.1% Segment), below the management-implied ~14.7%.
base.da_capex_rationale: Ex-REA FY26 D&A ~$401m (5.3%) includes amortisation of acquired intangibles (OPIS, CMA, Base Chemicals, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance deals) running above ex-REA capex of ~$332m (4.4%); D&A converges toward capex over the horizon. HarperCollins' new warehouse equipment is a $120m finance lease, outside capex.
base.tax_rationale: Ex-REA cash tax 25% flat: consolidated GAAP ETR 29%/30% is lifted by REA's 30% Australian rate; the remaining mix is ~60% US (21% federal + state), UK 25%, Australian News Media 30%. Consolidated cash taxes paid were $274m FY26 (26% of pre-tax), of which REA is roughly $200m, so the ex-REA cash rate has run below 25%; 25% is the normalised rate, not the trailing one.
base.wc_rationale: 0% capture: Dow Jones deferred revenue is a modest inflow on growth, HarperCollins receivables/inventory an outflow; FY26 consolidated working capital was -$145m and FY25 -$206m, FY24 -$139m, mostly REA receivables and book inventory. Treated as neutral on the ex-REA change in revenue.

bull.narrative: Dow Jones hits the $1bn EBITDA target on time (FY31) with Risk & Compliance compounding mid-teens and AI content licensing (OpenAI, Meta, Bloomberg) scaling as a near-100%-margin line; Move reaches a 10%+ margin on premium agent products; News Media's restructuring finishes and licensing revenue stabilises the segment. Adjusted margin reaches 15.5% (~16.6% Segment).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: two of the four ex-REA units (News Media, Move) are in structural or competitive retreat and the AI-traffic threat to Dow Jones' funnel is live and unresolved (Google subpoenas, publisher antitrust claims dismissed 30-Sep-2026). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: the $1bn Dow Jones target on schedule, AI licensing scaling beyond the announced deals, and Move turning profitable against Zillow. Base 50%. The REA stake is identical in all three scenarios, so the spread understates total downside if Australian housing turns; the bridge note gives the per-A$10 sensitivity.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
